name: European Statistics Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: audit and peer-review evidence on governance; no studies of economic effects
summary: The 2009 regulation is the legal basis for EU official statistics and the independence of statistical offices. The EU's auditors (2012) and peer reviews (2013-2015) found the quality code only partly applied, with over 700 recommendations, many on independence. A 2024 amendment giving statisticians access to private data is forecast to bring EUR 1.5 billion a year of benefits for EUR 757 million of costs; it has not yet been evaluated.

indicators.objective: The 2007 proposal has no indicators section; monitoring relies on the Code of Practice peer reviews and statistical programme evaluations

indicators.indicator: Compliance with the European Statistics Code of Practice
indicators.evidence: ECA 2012: Code not yet fully implemented, weak verification and enforcement. 2013-15 peer reviews: 707 recommendations (65 to achieve compliance), professional independence a recurring issue.

indicators.objective: Timely statistics using new data sources
indicators.indicator: Access to privately held and administrative data; crisis response
indicators.target_or_baseline: Benefits EUR 1.5bn/yr (EUR 577m to business) vs costs EUR 757m/yr
indicators.evidence: Amendment adopted as Regulation (EU) 2024/3018; evaluation due five years after implementation.

literature.citation: European Court of Auditors (2012), Did the Commission and Eurostat improve the process for producing reliable and credible European statistics?, Special Report No 12/2012
literature.title: Did the Commission and Eurostat improve the process for producing reliable and credible European statistics?
literature.headline: Commission and Eurostat had not yet achieved full implementation of the Code of Practice; Code demanding but lacks strong verification and enforcement tools; ambiguity over which elements are binding; statistical programme not an effective planning and accountability tool
literature.summary_plain: The EU's auditors found in 2012 that the rules meant to guarantee trustworthy EU statistics were not fully applied or enforced.

literature.citation: European Commission (2016), Report on the implementation of the European Statistics Code of Practice and coordination within the ESS, COM(2016) 114
literature.title: Report on the implementation of the European Statistics Code of Practice and coordination within the ESS
literature.method: peer reviews of all Member States, EFTA countries and Eurostat (2013-2015)
literature.headline: 707 peer-review recommendations (avg 21 per country), 65 needed to achieve compliance; professional independence (88 recommendations) and the need to revise statistical laws on appointment and dismissal of chief statisticians were main issues
literature.summary_plain: Independent peer reviews in 2013-2015 made over 700 recommendations, often about protecting statistical offices' independence.

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Impact assessment for the amendment of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 (executive summary SWD(2023) 241), SWD(2023) 240
literature.title: Impact assessment for the amendment of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 (executive summary SWD(2023) 241)
literature.headline: Statistics not timely, frequent, detailed or cost-efficient enough; preferred targeted revision: direct benefits EUR 1.5bn a year (EUR 577m for business) vs direct costs EUR 757m a year (EUR 196m for business); micro and small firms exempt from mandatory data sharing
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected giving statisticians access to private and administrative data to bring EUR 1.5 billion a year of benefits for EUR 757 million of costs.
